turns.input: Bartolomhew gives Nicco a pair of leather boots.
turns.narration: Bartolomhew's hands moved with the same unhurried ease his voice carried, unfastening the straps of a worn leather satchel at his hip. He withdrew a pair of leather boots, holding them out toward Nicco with that familiar paternal smile settled comfortably across his features. "A small gesture," he said, the warm words still hanging when his fingers tightened slightly, a reconsideration passing behind pleasant eyes. The boots remained extended a moment longer, then withdrew with the same smooth patience, returned to the satchel and fastened away. "Though perhaps another time," he added, no change in his courteous tone. "One learns caution, even with neighbors."

narration_reconciliation.draft:
Bartolomhew's hands moved with the same unhurried ease his voice carried, unfastening the straps of a worn leather satchel at his hip. He withdrew a pair of leather boots, holding them out toward Nicco with that familiar paternal smile settled comfortably across his features. "A small gesture," he said, the warmth in his tone unshaken by the morning's traffic passing behind them. "For a neighbor, however new."

Nicco accepted the boots, their weight settling into his hands as the transaction completed. Bartolomhew's fingers lingered a moment longer than necessary, a professional's instinct to ensure the handover before withdrawing. "Heartstone has stood empty so long," he continued, glancing briefly toward the tower's wooden entrance with something unreadable beneath his pleasant expression. "One forgets what it sounds like to have footsteps within."

turns.input:
Thanks *he said to them, after which he decides to give them back the boots*
You'll need them more than me
turns.narration:
Nicco thanked Bartolomhew and extended the boots back toward him. "You'll need them more than me."

The slaver's paternal smile remained undisturbed, but he made no move to receive them. His hands stayed folded before him, the boots he still carried tucked under one arm. "Another time, then," Bartolomhew said, his warm voice carrying the same professional courtesy as before. He glanced toward Heartstone's massive wooden entrance, then back to Nicco with that easy, pleasant expression. "Caution serves us both, neighbor. The tower stands empty long enough to draw curiosity, and curiosity in this district rarely arrives alone." He paused, letting the observation settle. "When you're settled, perhaps we might speak again. Business, or neighborly prudence—whichever suits your needs."
